title: Salon SEO Case Study: Lahore Website Rebuild | 22 Signals
description: Salon SEO case study: how we rebuilt a Lahore beauty salon's website, launched it in July 2026, started SEO on day one and planned Google Ads for brides.
h1: Salon SEO case study: a new website, search plan and Google Ads for a Lahore beauty salon
intro: This salon SEO case study follows a beauty salon and studio in Lahore. We audited its old website, researched the market and competitors, wrote the content, rebuilt the site and launched it on 14 July 2026, with SEO starting the same day. The salon then asked us to run Google Ads for bridal makeup searches.

p: The client is a beauty salon and studio in Lahore. It came to us needing two things at once: a rebuilt website and a search programme that would bring in people who did not already know its name.

Many businesses buy those as separate projects from separate suppliers. We think that is a mistake. A rebuild is the one moment when you decide which pages exist, what each page is for and which searches it should answer. If the developers build first and the SEO team arrives later, the new site often has to be reworked page by page. So we planned the build and the search work as one project with one lead.

list: An audit of the existing website, alongside strategy, market and competitor research, from 1 to 8 June 2026. The contract itself started on 8 June.
A keyword strategy and competitor analysis, so every planned page had a clear search it was written for.
Website content documents for each page, with strategy and content finalised on 12 June.
Site development from 15 June to 1 July.
Sitewide imagery, supplied by the salon's own team and put in place from 2 to 9 July.
Launch on 14 July, and the start of SEO that same day.
A rank tracker, a technical crawl and audit of the live site after launch, and a branded progress report for the owners.

p: One Signal Lead owned the project from the first call to launch and stayed on for the search work after it. The salon dealt with one person, not a designer, a developer and an SEO consultant each with their own view.

We worked in a fixed order: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow. Research came before any design. The words for each page were written and approved before development began, so the developers built around agreed content instead of placeholder text. The salon's team supplied the photography, and we slotted it in across the site once the build was stable.

Every date went in writing. Launch was booked for 13 July. A hosting delay pushed it back by one day, to 14 July, and we started SEO on launch day rather than waiting for a quiet week. When a plan moves, even by a day, we tell the client straight away and explain why.

sections.h: Search for people and for AI answers
p: The search work covered classic SEO, plus answer engine optimisation and generative engine optimisation: writing pages so that the services, location and specialities are stated plainly enough for Google and for AI assistants to describe the salon accurately.

In practice that means clear service pages, consistent business details, direct answers to the questions people ask before booking, and a technical base that crawlers can read without trouble. The post-launch crawl was there to check that the new build had not introduced problems the old site did not have.

The salon now has a rebuilt website, live since 14 July 2026, with content written against a keyword plan rather than guesswork. SEO has run since launch. Rankings are tracked, the live site has been audited, and the owners have a progress report that shows what was done and what comes next.
We are not publishing ranking figures or enquiry numbers for this client here. What we can say is what the engagement produced and when each piece shipped.

sections.h: The next stage: Google Ads for bridal makeup
p: With the site and SEO in place, the salon asked us to run Google Ads in Pakistan, aimed at people searching for bridal makeup. Bridal bookings matter to a salon, and paid search lets the business appear for those searches while organic rankings keep building.

Starting ads after the rebuild, not before, matters. Paid clicks are only worth buying when the page they land on is fast, clear and built to turn a visitor into a booking. The salon now has that page structure to send traffic to.

sections.h: What other salons and studios can take from this salon SEO case study
list: Plan the website and the search work together, before design starts.
Approve the words before the developers build the pages.
Use your own photography if you have it; it shows the real work.
Start SEO on launch day, and audit the live site straight after launch.
Add paid search once the landing pages are ready to convert.

p: Web Development for the rebuild, SEO and GEO for search and AI answers, Paid Media for the Google Ads phase, and Strategy and Go-to-Market for the opening research. If your salon or studio is in a similar position, book a 15-minute call and we will tell you honestly whether we are a fit.

author: Daniyal Mansur
